name: Riyad Capital
legal_name: Riyad Capital (a sole shareholder closed joint stock company)
founded: CMA licence 07070-37 dated 19 Jun 2007; CR 1010239234 dated 24 Oct 2007 (then an LLC); operations commenced February 2008 (AR 2025); became a closed joint stock company on 28 Feb 2017 (FS note 1).
ownership_summary: 100% owned by Riyad Bank: SAR 500m capital divided into 250 million shares (AR 2025; FS note 1). Statutory reserve SAR 150m. Riyad Bank filed in July 2025 to list part of the company on Tadawul; as of 12 Oct 2026 no approval, prospectus or listing was found.
government_link: Indirect. The parent, Riyad Bank, shows PIF 21.8% and GOSI 10.4% in its AR 2025 shareholder chart (see sa-riyad).
group_structure: 100% subsidiary of Riyad Bank (sa-riyad), reported as the bank's 'Investment banking and brokerage' segment. Double counting: Riyad Capital's balance sheet, income and AUM are consolidated in the bank; never add this record to sa-riyad. The segment (H1 2026 operating income SAR 493m; total assets SAR 4.67bn) is close to but not identical with the standalone firm. The company has no subsidiaries other than unnamed SPVs that safeguard fund assets (AR 2025); FS note 1 also mentions immaterial subsidiaries that are not consolidated. Siblings under Riyad Bank include Jeel Digital Innovation (technology), 1957 Ventures Fund (fintech VC) and Riyad Financial Markets (see sa-riyad). Riyad Bank provides some support services under service agreements.

business_lines: Asset management (public funds, private funds, DPM, real estate, private equity and venture capital, Global Money Market and Fixed Income); wealth management and investment advisory; brokerage (local, GCC, international, margin financing, institutional trading, algorithmic execution); securities services and custody (AUC over SAR 1tn, fund services, paying agent for sukuk); corporate investment banking (ECM, DCM, sukuk and bonds, structured finance, M&A); research. capabilities.wealth_summary: Riyad Capital is Riyad Bank's 100%-owned, CMA-licensed (07070-37) investment arm covering asset management, wealth management, brokerage, securities services and corporate investment banking. It managed SAR 97.5bn at end-2025 and SAR 101.3bn at 30 Jun 2026 (parent slide), and held SAR 1,048bn in custody (a record) at end-2025. FY2025 revenue was SAR 1,035m (first year above SAR 1bn; +16%) and net income SAR 664m, with asset management fees SAR 418m, brokerage SAR 348m and securities services SAR 70m. The shelf is mostly its own: 14 equity funds, 9 multi-asset funds (Shariah and conventional variants), fixed income and money market funds, REITs, real estate (over SAR 26bn), private equity and venture funds (over SAR 1.7bn), plus discretionary portfolios; advisory says funds are 'managed in-house and via 3rd party providers'. Retail investing runs in separate apps: Riyad Capital (Saudi market, with the 'Mostshary' goal-based planning service) and Riyad Global (US and international stocks, options and ETFs, login on clientam.com), both needing a Riyad Online login and a Riyad Capital account. Riyad Bank filed in July 2025 to list part of Riyad Capital on Tadawul (no approval found by 12 Oct 2026), and its board was reconstituted by 2026 under new chairman Waleed Fatani.

private_banking.detail: Private banking sits in the parent bank (Private Banking, Diamond, Golden, see sa-riyad). Riyad Capital has a Wealth Management division (Head: Abdulaziz AlRegaibah, an ex-Riyad Bank private and Golden banking professional) and a DPM service for 'institutional and high net-worth clients'; no eligibility thresholds published.

asset_management.detail: AUM SAR 97.5bn (31 Dec 2025), SAR 101.3bn (30 Jun 2026). Website: 14 equity funds, 9 multi-asset funds, fixed income, money market and REIT categories, DPM and private funds. 2025 launches: Riyad Fixed Income Funds 3 and 4 (private placements), Riyad Financing Fund 5, Riyad Monthly Distribution Multi-Asset Fund (over SAR 250m by year-end), five real estate funds. SAR Liquidity Fund grew over 300%; DPM AUM +50%; seven multi-asset funds in the top ten of their category; Riyad Al Jarei Fund topped public-fund performance. All funds and portfolios moved to Bloomberg AIM in 2025. FT Asset Management Excellence Awards Middle East 2025: Best Private Equity Manager.

brokerage.detail: Saudi market via Riyad Capital Online/Mobile and a new app with TradingView charts; GCC; international (23 markets listed incl. US, Canada, Mexico, Europe, Hong Kong, Australia, Singapore, Japan; stocks, bonds, options, ETFs; no annual account fee; a commission-free 'Lite' tier with extended US pre-market hours). H1 2026 value traded SAR 44.7bn (-30% YoY). 2025 additions: client rewards programme, face login, portfolio views for real estate funds and Murabaha, securities lending ('yield enhancement'), and an algorithmic trading system supporting HFT and market-making for institutions. Margin financing and IVR/ATM/centres channels. FY2025 brokerage commission SAR 347.7m (+24%). Market share not disclosed.

digital_investing.detail: 'Riyad Capital' app (iOS seller Riyad Capital; v2.0.5, 14 Jun 2026; first released 28 Aug 2022; 291 ratings, average 3.09): local trading, interactive charts (TickerChart and TradingView), watchlists, alerts, research, Mostshary planning, referral programme. 'Riyad Global' app (v10.07, 21 Sep 2026; first released 1 Mar 2019; 63 ratings, average 2.84): stocks, options and ETFs in global markets. Both require a Riyad Online login (same as the bank) and a Riyad Capital investment account; the website page does not list fund subscription or IPO in the apps. Investment account opening starts from Riyad Capital Online.

advisory.detail: Investment advisory for individuals and institutions through a 'specially developed advisory process', dedicated team of advisors, covering local and international equities; offers tailored portfolios, DPM, tailor-made structured products and CMA-registered funds. Chief Investment Officer's office publishes economic and investment views and runs all clients' multi-asset portfolios; research covers 50 listed companies (43 in 2024).

discretionary.detail: Discretionary Portfolio Management for institutional and high-net-worth clients, built on an Investment Policy Statement and Investment Management Agreement; DPM AUM grew over 50% in 2025 and the investable universe was widened to global equities and alternatives. No minimum or fees published.

model_portfolios_robo.detail: 'Mostashary' (Mostshary) robo-advisory service launched in 2025 uses Riyad Capital multi-asset funds as the investment tools, with three steps: goal, target amount and risk appetite (App Store description), 'providing users with diversified strategies aligned with their respective risk profiles' (AR 2025). Inside the Riyad Capital app; the website pages on apps and advisory do not mention it. Launch date, minimums and technology vendor not found.

funds_platform.detail: Advisory page states mutual funds are CMA-registered and 'managed in-house and via 3rd Party Providers'. The public funds pages list only Riyad-branded funds; no third-party fund platform provider or named third-party fund manager found.

structured_products.detail: Advisory offers 'tailor made structured products'; no product list, minimum or issuer named. Riyad Capital also advises corporates on structured finance (corporate investment banking).

private_markets.detail: Real estate: over SAR 26bn managed (83 properties in 18 cities across three continents), five funds launched in 2025. Private equity and venture capital: over SAR 1.7bn across five funds (Riyad Taqnia Fund, Riyad FinTech Fund, 1957 Ventures Fund, Riyad Venture Capital Opportunities Fund I investing in March Capital Partners Fund IV, Riyad Pre-IPO Opportunities Fund I). Led the 2025 round for Ninja (over SAR 1bn, unicorn status). Riyad Taqnia Fund exited investments for SAR 150m proceeds (gross TVPI 3x).

islamic_wealth.detail: Shariah-compliant variants across the shelf: Riyad Saudi Equity Sharia Fund, Riyad Global Equity Sharia Fund, Monthly Distribution multi-asset fund and Sharia versions of the four risk-profile multi-asset funds; the firm itself is not Shariah-only (conventional variants exist). An Annual Shariah Committee Report is published (file labelled 2024).

Asset management: Fixed Income Funds 3 and 4, Financing Fund 5, Monthly Distribution Multi-Asset Fund, five real estate funds, Mostashary robo-advisory launch, migration to Bloomberg AIM; led the Ninja pre-IPO round (over SAR 1bn)

Brokerage: TradingView, rewards programme, face login, portfolio views, securities yield enhancement, extended US pre-market for the Lite tier, algorithmic trading with HFT and market-making support; custody passed SAR 1 trillion
Corporate investment banking advised on six sukuk and bond deals worth SAR 30.3bn (incl. SAR 2bn Riyad Bank AT1 as sole lead) and the SAR 5.3bn Petro Rabigh capital increase; CIB fees fell 35%
FS 2025 authorised (Chairman Mohammed Al Joaid signing); by 12 Oct 2026 the board page shows a different seven-member board chaired by Waleed Fatani (no announcement found)

opportunities: Fragmented investor journey: Riyad Capital app (Saudi), Riyad Global (international) and a separate Riyad Dawli app/portal for GCC, each needing a Riyad Online login and a Riyad Capital account; the app page lists no fund subscription or IPO (S14, S11, S15)
App ratings are low on small samples: Riyad Capital app 3.09 on 291 ratings and Riyad Global 2.84 on 63 ratings (S20, S21)
Robo/planning ('Mostashary') exists but runs only on Riyad multi-asset funds, with no published portfolios, minimums or vendor (S6, S20)
Advisory page says funds are 'managed in-house and via 3rd Party Providers' (S12), while the public shelf found lists only Riyad-branded funds (S16, S17)
IPO filed with the CMA in July 2025 and the board was reconstituted in 2026, indicating a standalone-company build-out (S22, S3)
H1 2026 brokerage value traded fell 30% and segment profit fell 12%, increasing the case for recurring-fee wealth products (S7)
Strategy: 'the most digitally enabled financial services firm in Saudi Arabia' with a three-year plan on five pillars (S6 p.4, p.19)
barriers: Strong in-house investment team: CIO since 2014 (ex-Julius Baer/UBS), all funds and portfolios on Bloomberg AIM, own robo built on own funds (S2, S6)

Scale and captive distribution through Riyad Bank: apps use bank credentials, the wealth head is ex-Riyad Bank, the parent group generated SAR 75.6m of brokerage and SAR 46.7m of securities-services revenue, and the parent supplies IT support, marketing and HR under a SAR 28.9m service level agreement (S14, S2, S5)
International execution already sourced (apparently Interactive Brokers infrastructure) (S11)
IPO preparation and board change may delay new vendor decisions (inference, not stated in sources)

discrepancies.detail: AR 2025 lists a six-member board (Chairman Eng. Mohammed Owaidh Al-Joaid, Vice Chairman Basel Bin Jabr, Nadir Al-Koraya, Abdullah Al-Oraini, Hanadi AlSheikh, Jehad Alkadi); the FS were signed by Al Joaid in March 2026. The website (12 Oct 2026) lists seven members chaired by Waleed Fatani and keeps only Bin Jabr and Alkadi.
discrepancies.resolution: Used the website as current. No announcement of the reconstitution or its date was found; former members not recorded as people.

discrepancies.detail: The parent's file notes the CEO's earlier bio listed him as a Riyad Capital director; the current official bio and board page do not. Education per the official bio is as recorded.
discrepancies.resolution: Not recorded as a director. Minor.

discrepancies.detail: FS 2025 note 25 gives SAR 93.8bn; the parent's statements give SAR 93.6bn. Both give SAR 97.5bn for 2025.
discrepancies.resolution: Recorded only the agreed 2025 figure and the 2Q26 figure; 0.2bn difference unresolved.

discrepancies.detail: Parent segment total assets SAR 4,672,920k at 30 Jun 2026 and operating income SAR 492,959k for H1 2026 differ in scope from the standalone FS (total assets SAR 4,182,120k at 31 Dec 2025; FY2025 revenue SAR 1,035,007k).
discrepancies.resolution: Used the standalone FS as primary and recorded the segment figures as 'parent_segment_*' proxies.

discrepancies.detail: The App Store description and AR 2025 describe Mostshary/Mostashary in the Riyad Capital app; the website pages on mobile apps and advisory do not mention it. The parent's file recorded SAR 1.7m invested in its first month (from the bank's AR, not re-verified here).
discrepancies.resolution: Recorded as present; scale not recorded.

discrepancies.detail: Executive profile pages show 'Modified' dates from 7 days to 11 months before the check, so some titles may have changed after AR 2025; CFO and COO have held their roles since 2019 per the bios.

open_items: No 30 Jun 2026 standalone statements or AUM: Riyad Capital publishes annual statements only. Balance sheet and income are FY2025; H1 2026 AUM (SAR 101.3bn), brokerage value traded and segment figures come from the parent's presentation and interim statements (proxies, rounded for the slide data).

IPO status: filed with the CMA on 1 Jul 2025 (Riyad Bank statement). No approval, prospectus, pricing or listing found as of 12 Oct 2026; check Tadawul/CMA announcements (not fetched, Tadawul pages return 403).
Board reconstitution (Fatani chair; Koshak, Alsuwailem, Alghamdi, Altwaijri new vs AR 2025) has no announcement or date found; board committee composition per the website only.

LinkedIn checks for the CEO, CIO and asset management head returned no matching profiles; all marked 'Not verified'. One search snippet suggests Hans Peter Huber's tenure at 'four years' (MarketScreener, undated) versus 'since 2014' on the official bio; the official bio was used.

Whether Riyad Global uses Interactive Brokers infrastructure is inferred from the clientam.com login domain and IBEOS code only; commission schedule PDFs and the Riyad Dawli app were not opened. Riyad Capital's website does not describe fund subscription or IPO in the apps.
Fixed income, money market and REIT fund lists, fund minimums and the investment-centre list were not captured. Mostashary scale, launch date and vendor not found.
FS 2025 PDF text layer is garbled in the statements pages; figures were read from rendered pages. The parent's H1 2026 interim FS (image-only) was read via local OCR for note 14.
Two fetched pages reported a trailing 'Hidden' section (text artefact); ignored. KingEclient (2023 app build) comes from a search result only.
CMA authorised-persons register entry not checked directly; licence number from the firm's FS.
